why: of the end of the gut
the threads a mussel holds by
the blister beetle and beetle is judged a compound
the sideritis said to heal iron wounds
the sempervivum grown on the roof
the cloth worn on the legs
a suffix fragment and not a word
the element named only for itself
not able to be told apart
the hollow stone said to be found in eagle nests
the lasting hurt of a limb
the four sided figure with one pair parallel
the antirrhinum whose flower opens like a mouth
